evidence: Platts p. 444 explicitly gives Hindi candr-mā/candar-mā moon and analyses it as Sanskrit candra plus mās. The existing candramas parent preserves this full compound, distinct from candra alone. Retained ndr-m identifies the learned Sanskrit word in these Hindi attestations.

Platts p. 444 verifies the whole Hindi candr-mā/candar-mā moon compound. The Hindi survey candrama attestation (kannauji p. 64) is linked to Sanskrit candramas in this same validated batch and provides a provisional immediate regional donor for the other survey forms. Independent Sanskrit learning or another Indo-Aryan intermediary remains possible; the attestation locality is not asserted to be the historical source.
